**Repaired finding submitted (ok:true): compliant** — no redline, no comment, document text left byte-identical.

**What the repair consisted of:** the verifier's substantive review affirmed every element of the analysis, so no change of classification or evidence was warranted. I re-anchored the quote on the single sentence that carries the convenience right and moved the reconciliation of the failed deterministic check to the front of the rationale, so the record makes plain that "terminate ... for any reason" is a termination-for-convenience right and the miss is a literal-phrase regex artefact rather than a gap in the contract.

**Basis for compliance at the fallback:**
- **Convenience right present** — "for any reason" after the Initial Term on 90 days' notice, at the outer edge of the 60–90 day fallback window.
- **No lock-in** — 1-year Initial Term with 1-year renewals; the ">12 months without a convenience right" trigger never fires.
- **Mid-term bar is symmetric** — it equally stops Kubient leaving us, so not flaggable against our party.
- **No penalty** — Kubient keeps only fees earned while still performing during the notice period, inside the 3-months'-fees ceiling.
- **Not walk-away** — Kubient's right is on exactly 90 days, not fewer.

Sub-elements short of preferred (90 vs. 30 days; Kubient's right not confined to term end; no pro-rata prepaid refund, inapplicable under the §5 revenue-share) remain recorded in the rationale only.

One point worth flagging to the deal team outside this rule: the deterministic check will keep failing on this document because the clause never uses the words "for convenience." If that check gates reporting, the fix belongs in the check's phrase list, not in the contract — we should not open a redline on AP's behalf to satisfy a regex where the substantive right is already at fallback.
